summary: Source-anchored research for positional index path caveat. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: A 2019 demonstration creates {"parts.0.sku":1} and obtains FETCH over IXSCAN for {"parts.0.sku":"abc"}. Its scalar-at-that-position example reports isMultiKey:false. Treat this as a demonstrated schema-specific option, not a guarantee that every positional index is non-multikey. (low confidence)

The +N example reports isMultiKey:false for its scalar first-element sku path. Treat this as a property of that demonstrated schema; the article does not establish that every path containing a numeric component is necessarily non-multikey. (low confidence)

Wildcard indexes ignore array element positions when recording elements, but they can still support queries that include explicit array indices: MongoDB documents db.fleet.find( { "ship.captains.0.name": "Francis Drake" } ) as able to use the wildcard index. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md

Numeric dotted components can mean field names as well as positions. SERVER-27442 demonstrates that {"a.2":99} matches both {"a":[1,32,99]} and {"a":[{"2":99},1,2]}; wildcard planner code explicitly enumerates field-name and array-index interpretations. Avoid assuming positional syntax alone disambiguates heterogeneous arrays. (high confidence) Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-27442 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/planner_wildcard_helpers.cpp

An index restricted to parts.0.sku cannot stand in for an index supporting the any-element predicate parts.sku: the 2019 demonstration shows COLLSCAN for that broader predicate because the positional index omits other elements. (low confidence)

A wildcard index cannot support ship.coordinates.0.1 when coordinates contains arrays directly inside an array: it stores each inner array as a whole, and MongoDB fulfills such a query with a collection scan. The planner also declines to use a wildcard index when a positional path component that follows a multikey component is followed by another positional component, because the query might need to match by position inside a nested array. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/planner_wildcard_helpers.cpp

The inspected wildcard planner rejects a query path included through an array-index wildcard projection: for multikey a, projection {"a.0":1} treats 0 as a field name and cannot safely supply {"a.0.b":...} under array-position query semantics. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Wildcard query eligibility is limited to at most eight explicit array indices in a field path; this is not an eight-level document-indexing depth limit. Planner comments explain that numeric field-name versus array-index interpretations require exponential path enumeration. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/planner_wildcard_helpers.cpp

For a query that targets a specific known positional array element, an index on that positional path (for example parts.0.sku) can be used, as shown by explain; queries without the positional path (parts.sku) do not use it and fall back to a collection scan. Sources: https://www.plusnconsulting.com/post/Positional-Array-Indexing-in-MongoDB/index.html

Do not assume an index on array supplies useful bounds for array.2. A MongoDB multikey index only indexes the values of the array, not their positions, so an ordinary index on array does not support queries on a specific position such as array.2; a workaround is to store explicit position keys and query with $elemMatch. Sources: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49134851/indexing-mongodb-array-position-queries

SERVER-119604 reports different results for {"A.0.B":{$ne:null}} before and after index creation and after inserting an empty array on MongoDB 8.0.19. The ticket was resolved Works as Designed on March 19, 2026; this is a reported version-specific reproduction, not an independently reproduced universal index bug. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-19)

In section 8.4, UC Berkeley researchers distinguish any-element queries from fixed-position queries in Arx, maintaining a separate names.0 index for the latter. Their prototype targets MongoDB 3.0; this corroborates the conceptual distinction but does not establish current MongoDB planner behavior. (low confidence)
